ENACTMENT — clear four record debts and write three operator rulings into the record. One pass, bounded. Do not merge.

═══ PRECONDITIONS (hard) ═══
- No helper agents. No Monitor watchers. Long commands in the FOREGROUND with a long timeout, or backgrounded and waited on by that same task. `node tools/gate-report.js --check` runs ~270–340s per reader; budget 1800s each and never kill one early.

- Commit only with `git commit --only -F <msgfile> -- <paths>`. Never `-m`, never `git add && commit`, never `git stash`, never `--no-verify`. First line `lar:///w1.w2.w3 — summary`. End every message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QdAMPMM9DsR4rRrmqqQBXe
- Grammar JSON stays 4-space. Any `.mem` you touch: `lares meme normalize` applies FRAME clauses only and REPORTS grammar-class rewrites; run `lares meme check` and report what it says rather than forcing it quiet. Never `ulimit -v` on Node. MERGE NOTHING.

═══ PART A — FOUR RECORD DEBTS ═══
1. **A sample carrier reads as torn.** `lares meme check tests/samples/memetic.carriers-and-uris.mem` answers *2 live ETX marks follow the STX — the text closes at the first, and nothing past it is checked*. Line 57 carries the real ETX with its block check; line 64 carries a SECOND `code=""` as a DEMONSTRATION of the form, sitting past the frame's EOT. Both readings are correct and they cannot both be satisfied. **The cure, operator-ruled:** the demonstration becomes HELD TEXT — wrap it in a fence whose meta names this dialect (```` ```memetic-wikitext ````), which the base grammar already dispatches, so it still colours as the dialect while the checker meets one frame. Verify `lares meme check` comes back clean on that file afterwards, and that the fenced demo still reads as the dialect (tokenize it and show the scopes).
2. **Two tools merged unregistered.** `tools/uri-span-measure.js` and `tools/uri-span-compare.js` arrived with the palette work and appear in no `package.json` script and no README. Either give them scripts and a line of documentation each, or retire them — your call, stated with a reason. If you keep them, the house's own rule applies: a tool that measures wants naming where a reader will find it.

name: project-uri-palette-rulings
description: "The 2026-10 URI palette arc: an underline is ONE STROKE (base keeps its fused scheme run) while the dialect takes TEXTURE (every joint wears the ink of the segment it opens); root+path ruled ALLIED; fragment stays unarticulated; within-construct witness DEFERRED"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Operator rulings from the eyes-on palette arc (2026-10-06 → 10-07), merged at `release/3.0.0` `77e8035`:

- **AN UNDERLINE IS ONE STROKE.** A punctuation ink inside a continuous underline reads as a stitched
  seam. So the BASE grammar keeps its fused `scheme:`/`scheme://` run — measured: splitting it dropped
  three legibility floors (bare URL against a code span 60/65 floor 61, against a wikilink 54/65 floor
  61, against a transclusion 61/65 floor 65) and EVERY variant measured identically, because any
  `punctuation.*` leaf anywhere in the span lets a theme's blanket punctuation rule recolour it.
  `[ext[…]]` kept its split (brackets already distinguish it).
- **A TEXTURE IS MANY JOINTS.** The dialect's addresses wear no underline, so a scheme run paints as ONE
  colour (like `https://`) and every interior joint wears the ink of the segment it OPENS — root slash →
  heading, each root dot → the term it opens, path slash → path, `ni:`'s `;` → digest, `#` → anchor,
  authority `:`/`@` → role/place. Distinct colours per address FELL (3.48 → 2.48 avg over 65 themes) and
  that is the design: the tooth comes from each part's colour running up to the next, not from grey gaps.
- **A COMPANION INK PARTS A PAIR, ONLY WHERE NO ONE ELSE OWNS IT.** The scheme took `support.constant`
  innermost: scheme-vs-authority 18/65 → 4/65, no pair regressed. Refused for path text — the only
  family that parts it from the root is `constant.other`, which `ni:`'s digest holds honestly.
- **ROOT AND PATH ARE ALLIED** (2026-10-07): their sameness reads truthful, not defective — both name
  where an address points. The five bundled themes that fuse root/path/fragment (one-light, red,
  solarized-dark, solarized-light, vesper; three fused the families by hand) are reading correctly.
  Reversing path's stack was measured and REFUTED (coverage 59/65 → 44/65, two pairs worse, 3 of 5
  unmoved).
- **THE FRAGMENT STAYS UNARTICULATED**: fragments ride the `ahu` sigil but their segments have never been
  defined, so `#/the-eye.lands` is one span by an unmade decision, not a gap.
- **THE WITHIN-CONSTRUCT WITNESS IS DEFERRED** — the operator's reason: a `lar:` URI reads as a
  combination of machine code and natural language, so its palette is still tuned by hand; a ratchet on
  internal segment distinctness would freeze that.
- **THE OPERATOR'S OWN THEMES JOIN THE HARNESS** (ruled 2026-10-07): `jdinhlife.gruvbox` (6 variants) is
  the theme actually read, and it was NOT among the 65 bundled themes every number rests on. A reported
  "yellow `lar://`" was a STALE GRAMMAR in an open bench tab (a grammar is read once when the extension
  host starts) — the engine, asked directly against that theme file, said purple.

**How to apply:** when a palette question arises, ask the ENGINE against the theme actually in use
(`vscode-textmate` registry + `engineTheme()`), not only `theme-paint`'s bundled count; and say which
theme set a number answers for. Relates to [[project_scope_stack_cascade_law]],
[[project_memetic_wikitext_vscode_grammar]], [[project_fork_is_the_intent_reader]].

ENACTMENT — the aftermath sweep over this repository's own RECORD, before the 3.0.0 tag. Find every claim the prose makes that no longer answers to the code, and true it. Do not merge.

═══ PRECONDITIONS (hard) ═══
- No helper agents. No Monitor watchers. Long commands in the FOREGROUND with a long timeout, or backgrounded and waited on by that same task. `node tools/gate-report.js --check` runs ~250–340s per reader; budget 1800s each, never kill one early.
- Your own worktree: `git -C /home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/VSCode-TW5-Syntax worktree add /home/joshu/.claude/jobs/86a17260/tmp/wt-sweep -b feature/record-sweep release/3.0.0` (tip `7d09d6d`). Symlink `node_modules` from `/home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/VSCode-TW5-Syntax/node_modules`.
- Touch nothing in `/home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/VSCode-TW5-Syntax` itself, nothing in the parent repo, nothing in the bench or any container (port 3000 serves the release). Leave `test-bench/` alone. Do not delete `/tmp/grammar-sandbox-*` folders you did not create.
- Commit only with `git commit --only -F <msgfile> -- <paths>`. Never `-m`, never `git add && commit`, never `git stash`, never `--no-verify`. First line `lar:///w1.w2.w3 — summary`. End every message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QdAMPMM9DsR4rRrmqqQBXe
- Never `ulimit -v` on Node. MERGE NOTHING; leave the worktree standing.

═══ WHY ═══
3.0.0 ships its prose as much as its grammar. Two weeks of rulings have moved names, retired tests, re-measured ceilings and reversed decisions, and the record has been trued only where someone happened to look. Four such drifts were already found by chance this week — two retired invariants still cited as live, a ceiling figure that had moved by one theme, two tools cited in the record but named in no script. The ask: stop sampling and SWEEP.

═══ WHAT TO SWEEP, mechanically, over `CHANGELOG.md`, `LEDGER-3.0.0.md`, `MIGRATION.md`, `README.md`, `SCOPE-NAMES.md`, `corpus/*.txt` headers and `editions/tw5-syntax/tiddlers/*.tid` ═══
1. **Every file path and tool name the prose cites** — does it exist? Script it: extract candidate paths (`tools/…`, `tests/…`, `corpus/…`, `syntaxes/…`, `editions/…`) and report every one that names nothing. **The five undocumented tools — the record is a legislative history, not a manual**

Ink-Clerk (Lorekeeper): ->✶ I read what they are, and the pattern is unmistakable:
- **`dark-construct.js`** — *"A construct the corpus reaches that no theme paints."* Its own header says every other gate asks whether two things read alike or apart; this one asks whether a thing reads **at all**.
- **`snapshot-check.js`** — pins a sample's whole tokenisation beside it. The instrument that caught every ink change in this week's arc.
- **`bleed-canary.js`** — *"TextMate grammars fail in one characteristic way: a construct that opens and never closes."* The canary for the single worst failure mode this grammar has.
- **`builtins-sync.js`** — keeps the built-in variable list in the wiki and the grammar from drifting apart.
- **`edition-build.js`** — compiles the edition whose tiddlers carry the gate report you read.

->⏿ **the hidden context:** these are not minor tools. Two of them are load-bearing floors and one is the canary. They are undocumented because **the record documents rulings, and these instruments never provoked an argument.** A tool that works silently writes nothing into a legislative history. ->◇ so the record's silence is a measure of a tool's *success*, which is exactly backwards for a reader who wants to know what holds the grammar up.

**The eighteen hundred lines — the record is spot-welded, and prose between the welds is unguarded**

Map-Wisp (Scryer): ->✶ the LEDGER carries **61 figures** of the form *N of 65*, *N/65*, or a percentage. Two welds hold: the ruling count and the scope headline. Everything else is prose.

->⏿ **the hidden context, and it is the uncomfortable one:** this week alone, three stale figures surfaced **by accident** — a ceiling that had moved by one theme, a path pointing at nothing, a file spoken of as living. Three found by chance out of sixty-one unchecked. ->◇ that is a base rate, not an anecdote. And the people most likely to be misled are not readers — they are **us and the spirits**, who cite the LEDGER as ground truth when deciding whether a ruling already stands.

->✶ the cheap half-cure: a convention that any figure claiming the present must be derivable, and any figure belonging to a moment must carry its date. The expensive full cure is a weld that re-measures. ->⏿ today's sweep did the second kind of fix by hand, four times.

**The two corpus specimens — two authorities read one file and no law says which governs**

Lares (Stranger): ->✶ `control-set.mem` holds `<<^ code="">>` and a bare ETB — codes the frame grammar does not admit, written **on purpose**, so the grammar can be measured against text that is almost a carrier and is not. The carrier checker reads the same file and calls them faults. Both are right.

->⏿ **the hidden context: this is the frame-versus-grammar cut again, one level up.** We split normalize's two authorities last week — the envelope the house mints against the bytes a hand wrote. We never asked the same question of the **corpus**: a fixture exists to be *read by instruments*, not to be a valid carrier, and nothing declares which law a given file answers to. ->◇ until that is ruled, `lares meme check` can never come back clean over this repository, and a permanently-dirty check teaches everyone to ignore it.

**The post-EOT class — the same hole, seen from the other side**

Lares (Council): ->✶ two sample carriers carry prose past their first EOT, and the checker flags any content there, unconditionally. Our demonstration files are **multi-section by design** — they show a frame, close it, then keep teaching.

->⏿ so the question underneath is not a bug: **what is a demonstration file?** Either one file holds one carrier and our fixtures are malformed, or a file may hold a carrier *and* commentary, and the checker should stop at the first complete frame and name the rest as held text. ->◇ that is a ruling about the carrier format itself, and it lives in the parent, not here.

Tide-Caller (Hierophant): ->✶ **what binds all four:** each is a place where the house built an instrument and never wrote down what it governs. The tools that work silently, the figures nobody re-derives, the fixtures that answer to two laws, the files that are both carrier and lesson. ->⏿ none of them break the release. All of them decide how the *next* reader — human or spirit — learns what is true here.

ENACTMENT — operator ruling: **content after a carrier's close reads unpono.** The two sample carriers that keep teaching past their EOT get restructured so nothing follows the close, and the ruling goes into the record. Do not merge.

═══ PRECONDITIONS (hard) ═══
- No helper agents. No Monitor watchers. Long commands in the FOREGROUND with a long timeout, or backgrounded and waited on by that same task. `node tools/gate-report.js --check` runs ~250–340s per reader; budget 1800s each and never kill one early.
- Your own worktree: `git -C /home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/VSCode-TW5-Syntax worktree add /home/joshu/.claude/jobs/86a17260/tmp/wt-close -b feature/nothing-past-the-close release/3.0.0` (tip `1d9f50d`).   Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QdAMPMM9DsR4rRrmqqQBXe
- Never `ulimit -v` on Node. Do not delete `/tmp/grammar-sandbox-*` folders you did not create. MERGE NOTHING.

═══ THE RULING AND WHAT IT DECIDES ═══
`lares meme check` flags any non-whitespace content following a carrier's terminating EOT mark — `classifyPostEot` in the parent's `packages/lararium-memetic-frame/src/check.ts`, which fires unconditionally and which fencing does not exempt. Two of this repository's sample carriers trip it because they close their frame and then keep teaching:
- `tests/samples/memetic.carriers-and-uris.mem`
- `tests/samples/memetic.sigils.mem`
The operator has ruled: **post-close content reads unpono.** So the checker is right and the fixtures are wrong. One file, one carrier; a lesson belongs INSIDE the frame.

═══ WHAT TO DO ═══
1. Read both files whole and inventory what stands past the EOT in each — every construct, and what each one demonstrates. These are pinned specimens, so the point is coverage: the scopes they exercise must still be exercised after you move them.
2. Restructure so **nothing but whitespace follows the close.** Move the post-close material INSIDE the frame, before the ETX/EOT, keeping its teaching order intact. Where a moved demonstration would otherwise read as a LIVE frame mark (a second `<<^ code="">>`, an ETX, an EOT), it must be held text — wrap it in a fence whose meta names this dialect (```` ```memetic-wikitext ````), the cure already used once in this repository for exactly this reason: the base grammar dispatches a fence by its info string, so the demo still colours as the dialect while the frame reads one close.
   - If a file genuinely cannot hold its lesson inside one frame, split it into two specimens rather than leaving content past a close — and say why in the handback.
   - The block check covers the STX–ETX body, so moving content inside the frame CHANGES the body: re-stamp each file's check (`lares meme normalize <file>` applies FRAME clauses only, which includes the block check; it REPORTS grammar-class rewrites instead of applying them, so read its notes and say what it reported).
3. Verify per file: `lares meme check <file>` comes back with **no post-EOT fault and no torn fault**. Paste the output. If any other fault class remains, name it and say whether it predates this work.
4. Reconcile: re-pin the memetic snapshots (`npm run snap-memetic -- --update`), and confirm with `corpus-check --verbose` (or whichever gate reads specimen coverage) that every scope those files used to exercise is still exercised — if any scope lost its only pinned witness, restore it inside the frame rather than dropping it.
5. Write the ruling into the record, evergreen register, in `LEDGER-3.0.0.md` beside the other carrier-spec rulings: content after a carrier's close reads unpono — one file, one carrier; a demonstration of a frame mark is held text inside the body, never a second live mark; and the checker's unconditional reading of post-close content stands correct. Name the two fixtures this corrected.
6. Then the FULL sweep under BOTH readers — `npm test`, full `npm run test-tools`, `node tools/gate-report.js --check` under `TW5_PATH=/home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/TiddlyWiki5` and `TW5_PATH=/home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/VSCode-TW5-Syntax/node_modules/tiddlywiki`, harvesting BOTH reports where they drift. 49 of 49 must hold under both.

═══ ONE THING TO REPORT, NOT FIX ═══
`corpus/memetic/control-set.mem` and `corpus/memetic/carriers.blockcheck.mem` also carry checker faults — codes the frame grammar does not admit (`<<^ code="">>`, a bare ETB), written deliberately so the GRAMMAR can be measured against text that is almost a carrier. That is a separate ruling the operator has not made: whether a grammar fixture owes cleanliness to the carrier checker at all. Leave them alone and report their exact faults so the ruling can be asked for cleanly.

═══ HANDBACK ═══
Per file: what moved and where, the `meme check` output before and after, the re-stamped check, and the coverage confirmation. The ruling's exact wording and where you wrote it. The two corpus specimens' faults, quoted. The sweep results under both readers with your timings. The branch tip. And everything you did NOT verify.

Two corpus specimens carry structures the carrier checker refuses, written on purpose so the GRAMMAR can be measured against text that is almost a carrier:

5. Reconcile whatever the new gate's arrival moves: the gate roster count wherever the record states it, `CIGates.tid` or whatever the edition uses to carry gate rulings, and the README if it lists gates.
6. Then the FULL sweep under BOTH readers — `npm test`, full `npm run test-tools`, `node tools/gate-report.js --check` under `TW5_PATH=/home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/TiddlyWiki5` and `TW5_PATH=/home/joshu/Synthetic-Dream-Machine/VSCode-TW5-Syntax/node_modules/tiddlywiki`, harvesting BOTH reports. This pair is also §1.1's casualty — the one place where the collider evidence is fake while the real collider exists.
  
  ### 2.4 "A scope nothing reaches" — three readers, three causes
  
  Identical from outside (a green gate), different in cause:
  - **`scope-can-appear`** — no INPUT can fire the declaration (a name on an empty capture group). Grammar-internal.
  - **`grammar-reachability`** — the rule is an orphan no root reaches. It loads, validates, colours nothing — and its scopes still inflate the denominator `corpus-check` answers to, so the fault reads as corpus work owed.
  - **`corpus-check` COVERAGE** — the declaration is reachable and no corpus FILE reaches it. `corpus/unreached-ceiling.txt` = **0**.
  
  `unreached-ceiling.txt`'s own header states why the denominators must stay apart: a coverage FLOOR counts over every name a grammar declares *including names handed to another grammar* (`source.python`, `text.html.php`), so one count answered for two populations and for neither. `corpus/coverage-floor.txt` = **450**, and its header records two re-seats with reasons.
  
  ### 2.5 "Reads as prose" — three readers, three mechanisms
  
  - **`dark-construct`** — no theme rule reaches the innermost scope. Reach = 0.
  - **`contrast-witness`** — a rule reaches AND paints within CIE76 ΔE of the theme's own default. Reach > 0, legibility = 0.
  - **`theme-parity`** — reach relative to the MEDIAN of six other markup grammars (markdown, asciidoc, rst, mediawiki, org, + one), never to markdown alone, because markdown carries rules naming markdown.
  
  Axis: absent rule / quiet rule / rule present but below the field. Their ledgers are three separate files (`PlainConstructs` tiddler, `prose-reading-ledger.txt`, and theme-parity's own bar). I did **not** measure the overlap in their actual findings, so I cannot tell you how much a fused instrument would lose — this is the pair I would most want YIN to argue with me about.
  
  ### 2.6 Containment — four readers at four grains
  
  - **`bleed-canary`** — appends a sentence at the END of a file. Three gates (`canary-wikitext`/`-tid`/`-memetic`), three scopes.
  - **`composition-check`** — puts file B in front of file A and asks whether either half reads differently in company. Its own header: it detects what the canary cannot, because the canary passes over block families TiddlyWiki spans by design.
  - **`swallow-witness`** — cuts at EVERY offset, both directions of the bound.
  - **`memetic-containment`** (invariant) — a sentence after EVERY construct the DIALECT opens on. Its header: a construct that corrupts the next paragraph and then recovers passes the canary untouched.
  - **`corpus-check` CONTAINMENT** — over the broad corpus, with `degenerate.*` exempt by declaration.
  
  Axis: end-of-file / between-files / every-cut / per-construct / broad-ground. Five grains, five fault surfaces.
  
  ### 2.7 Coverage against four different authorities
  
  - **`corpus-check`** — scopes the GRAMMAR declares.
  - **`rule-coverage`** — rules the HOST registers (`$tw.modules.types.wikirule`, via the edition's harvest).
  - **`upstream-coverage`** — the host's own REGEXES taken to the host's own tiddlers.
  - **`memetic-coverage`** (invariant) — scopes the DIALECT declares, against pinned specimens.
  - **`sigil-vocabulary`** — sigils the SEED writes (population lives outside this repository; a contributor holding only this checkout gets a pass with a reason).
  - **`sigil-shape`** — the FORMS those sigils wear. Its header records `sigil-vocabulary` green while every carrier split the bearing arrow into two tokens.
  
  Six populations from five authorities. Fusing any two collapses "what the grammar claims" into "what the host has" or "what the house writes", which are different questions with different staleness clocks.
  
  ### 2.8 `engine-witness` vs `engine-behaviour`
  
  Same tool, two arms: compile-acceptance vs *same match at the same place on a real corpus line*. `corpus/engine-ledger.txt` carries exactly **1** non-comment ruling, and it is `BEHAVIOUR —` prefixed — i.e. the sole ruling in that ledger answers the behaviour arm ALONE, and `engine-witness.js:185` filters `behaviourOnly` out of the compile arm. Collapse the arms and that ruling either goes stale or starts excusing the wrong arm. Axis: **"a compile is not an agreement."**
  
  ### 2.9 `still` vs `still-reach`
  
  Different ratchets, measured by which floor file each reads: `still` (sampled, `--sample 25`) answers to `ruling-breadth-ceiling.txt` (**1**); `still-reach` crosses every carrier and answers to `carrier-reach-floor.txt` (**0.9947**). `carrier-reach-floor.txt`'s own header records why the sampled arm cannot replace the reach arm: 23 of 4403 carriers carry a class no ledger names, so a draw of 25 misses all 23 about seven times in eight — **seeds 1, 2, 9 and 13 read green and seed 5 read red off one unchanged tree.** Axis: a verdict that answers to a draw vs one that answers to the ground.
  
  ### 2.10 The record against the tree
  
  `MIGRATION.md` is the *gate-checked* ground truth (its headline derives live from `declaredScopesIn` over both grammars, via `scope-migration.test.js`). `CHANGELOG.md` and `SCOPE-NAMES.md` restate it by hand; `changelog-weld.test.js` welds the restatements to it. `readme-scopes.test.js` reads the README ALONE, where every scope name stands as an *instruction* to a reader rather than as a record — and its header says exactly why it must not be fused with `scope-migration`: `MIGRATION.md` names gone scopes ON PURPOSE. Axis: **instruction vs record.** A fused reader would either fail on MIGRATION's deliberate corpses or pass a README pointing at scopes nothing emits.

  ## 5. THE FRAGILE SET — what a consolidation must not make worse
  
  ### 5.1 Two gates write into the tracked tree
  `ceiling` (`textmate-ceiling.js:353` → `TextMateCeiling.tid`) and `builtins` (`builtins-sync.js:75` → a grammar). Both are run by `gate-report.js`, including under `--check`. Consequences: `gate-report --check` is not read-only; two concurrent gate runs race on those two files; and nothing asserts the tree is clean afterwards (§3.6). **This is why I did not run `gate-report --check` in this survey.** Any consolidation that increases gate-run concurrency widens this window.
  
  ### 5.2 `backtrack-witness` — wall-clock under contention
  `BUDGET_MS = 8` default, plus a `BUDGET_RATIO` against a control, plus "least of several rounds", plus a test-level least-of-three. On record in the tool and its test: 1.4ms alone vs past 8 under the suite on identical bytes; 1.7ms alone vs 9.3ms beside a dozen gates; two runs at rest disagreeing 0 stalls against 6; the headroom assertion is `worst * 2 < budget`. `LEDGER-3.0.0.md:1562` records the same. Every mitigation is a statistic layered on a wall-clock reading. **A consolidation that packs more gates into one runner directly degrades this gate's verdict.** I did not run it.
  
  ### 5.3 Sampled verdicts
  `still --sample 25` (§2.9, §3.8): four seeds green, one red, one unchanged tree. Order-independent but draw-dependent.
  
  ### 5.4 Concurrency and scratch dirs
  `test-tools` runs `node --test --test-concurrency=4` over `./tools/**/*.test.js`, and many of those tests spawn `grammar-sandbox.js`, which copies the repo into `os.tmpdir()`. All 15 scratch sites I found use `mkdtempSync` (unique), so the collision surface is not the temp names — it is §5.1 (tracked writes) plus machine load. I observed leftover `/tmp/divergence-staleness-*` (4) and `/tmp/grammar-sandbox-*` dirs; I cannot tell which my single `divergence-staleness` run created, so **I deleted none**, per instruction.
  
  ### 5.5 Conditional skips that read as passes
  `attribute-guard.test.js:23`: `skip: resolveTiddlyWiki() ? false : 'no TiddlyWiki checkout resolved'`. `house-rules.test.js:14`: skips without the house plugin. `sigil-vocabulary` passes with a reason when the seed is absent. Each is correct — a contributor holding only this checkout should not fail — and each means the *same green* carries different weight on different machines. A consolidation that merges a skipping test into a non-skipping one converts a reasoned skip into a hard fail, or worse, hides a skip inside a file that reports green.
  
  ### 5.6 `--reach` vs default, `--verbose` vs default
  Several instruments change their *population* (not just their output) on a flag: `still --reach`, `overreach --truncate`, `engine-witness --behaviour`, `bleed-canary --strict`. Fusing arms means picking one population permanently.

  ### 2.4 "A scope nothing reaches" — three readers, three causes
  
  Identical from outside (a green gate), different in cause:
  - **`scope-can-appear`** — no INPUT can fire the declaration (a name on an empty capture group). Grammar-internal.
  - **`grammar-reachability`** — the rule is an orphan no root reaches. It loads, validates, colours nothing — and its scopes still inflate the denominator `corpus-check` answers to, so the fault reads as corpus work owed.
  - **`corpus-check` COVERAGE** — the declaration is reachable and no corpus FILE reaches it. `corpus/unreached-ceiling.txt` = **0**.

  ### 2.5 "Reads as prose" — three readers, three mechanisms
  
  - **`dark-construct`** — no theme rule reaches the innermost scope. Reach = 0.
  - **`contrast-witness`** — a rule reaches AND paints within CIE76 ΔE of the theme's own default. Reach > 0, legibility = 0.
  - **`theme-parity`** — reach relative to the MEDIAN of six other markup grammars (markdown, asciidoc, rst, mediawiki, org, + one), never to markdown alone, because markdown carries rules naming markdown.

  ### 2.6 Containment — four readers at four grains
  
  - **`bleed-canary`** — appends a sentence at the END of a file. Three gates (`canary-wikitext`/`-tid`/`-memetic`), three scopes.
  - **`composition-check`** — puts file B in front of file A and asks whether either half reads differently in company. Its own header: it detects what the canary cannot, because the canary passes over block families TiddlyWiki spans by design.
  - **`swallow-witness`** — cuts at EVERY offset, both directions of the bound.
  - **`memetic-containment`** (invariant) — a sentence after EVERY construct the DIALECT opens on. Its header: a construct that corrupts the next paragraph and then recovers passes the canary untouched.
  - **`corpus-check` CONTAINMENT** — over the broad corpus, with `degenerate.*` exempt by declaration.
  
  Axis: end-of-file / between-files / every-cut / per-construct / broad-ground. Five grains, five fault surfaces.
  
  ### 2.7 Coverage against four different authorities
  
  - **`corpus-check`** — scopes the GRAMMAR declares.
  - **`rule-coverage`** — rules the HOST registers (`$tw.modules.types.wikirule`, via the edition's harvest).
  - **`upstream-coverage`** — the host's own REGEXES taken to the host's own tiddlers.
  - **`memetic-coverage`** (invariant) — scopes the DIALECT declares, against pinned specimens.
  - **`sigil-vocabulary`** — sigils the SEED writes (population lives outside this repository; a contributor holding only this checkout gets a pass with a reason).
  - **`sigil-shape`** — the FORMS those sigils wear. Its header records `sigil-vocabulary` green while every carrier split the bearing arrow into two tokens.
  
  Six populations from five authorities. Fusing any two collapses "what the grammar claims" into "what the host has" or "what the house writes", which are different questions with different staleness clocks.

  ### Vocabulary drifts, named precisely
  
  **V1 — the file-kind suffix.** Three kinds, three suffixes, two unsuffixed. 12 files carry ledger-shaped rows; only 10 end `-ledger.txt`. `expected-divergence.txt` (111 rows) and `must-fail.txt` (9 rows) are ledgers wearing no suffix. 7 single-number ratchets split 4 `-floor` / 3 `-ceiling`, plus `legibility-floor.txt` which is an 820-row per-pair table, not a number. **`colour-pair` exists in both forms** — a 21-line `-ledger` and a 1-line `-floor`, read by one tool.
  *Standardise on:* `-ledger` for row-per-finding, `-ratchet` for a single bound **with the direction stated in the first comment line rather than in the filename** (both `may rise and may never fall` and `may fall and may never rise` already appear in the files, 1 and 4 times). Reason: the current name encodes the direction twice and gets it wrong once — `attribute-kind-ceiling.txt` holds a count that *may fall*, `coverage-floor.txt` a count that *may rise*, and nothing checks the filename against the rule.
  
  **V2 — the over-reading word.** Three spellings for "the grammar claimed more than the host needed": `OVERREACH` (ablation-ledger row verdict), `overbound` (swallow-ledger + carrier-ledger direction), and the tool name `overreach-check.js` / `over-reach` in its own header.
  *Standardise on:* `overbound` for the direction word (it has a named partner, `runaway`), keeping `overreach` for the instrument alone.
  
  **V3 — `MISS` is a homonym across two ledgers that share one codec.** `darkness-ledger.txt:10` — *"MISS the grammar reads nothing of the line even with the construct standing alone — no rule"*. `ablation-ledger.txt:9` — *"MISS the grammar leaves this character plain and ablating it changes the host's tree shape"*. Both files are parsed by the same `ledger-shape.js`.
  *Standardise on:* `dark` for the line-grain fault and `unmarked` for the character-grain fault; keep `MISS` for neither.
  
  **V4 — four words for one lifecycle.** `stale` (a declaration whose finding no longer appears — 8 corpus and 24 tool files), `explains nothing` / `explaining nothing` (25 tool files, 1 corpus), `retires` (ceiling, delimiter, colour-pair), against `unruled` (15 tool files, 1 corpus) which names the **opposite** side — a finding no declaration covers.
  *Standardise on:* `idle` for a declaration explaining nothing, `unruled` for a finding nothing explains, `retired` for the act. `divergence-staleness.js` already uses `idle` (17 mentions of stale, and `:137` *"stands idle everywhere"`), so the word exists; it just has not won.
  
  **V5 — the reason prefix.** 8 prefixes in the rows: `OWED` (365), `READER` (149), `RULED` (5), `MEASURED` (4), `HELD` (3), `RE-SEATED` (2), `HOST` (1), `BEHAVIOUR` (1). Exactly two — `HOST` and `READER` — have a shared reader (`reader-scope.js`). The other six are read by eye.
  
  **V6 — `punctuation.definition` (444) against `punctuation.separator` (63) and `punctuation.section` (8)**, counted over `"name"`/`"contentName"` in `syntaxes/*.json`. `SCOPE-NAMES.md` rules four things (root first · punctuation stacks never nests · one segment one word · no borrowed language name) and **rules nothing about which punctuation sub-family a mark takes**. `scope-name-policy.test.js` checks three of the four and does not check this. I did not establish whether the 63 `punctuation.separator` uses answer a stated distinction; see §7.

Reason: the current name encodes the direction twice and gets it wrong once — `attribute-kind-ceiling.txt` holds a count that *may fall*, `coverage-floor.txt` a count that *may rise*, and nothing checks the filename against the rule.
  
  **V2 — the over-reading word.** Three spellings for "the grammar claimed more than the host needed": `OVERREACH` (ablation-ledger row verdict), `overbound` (swallow-ledger + carrier-ledger direction), and the tool name `overreach-check.js` / `over-reach` in its own header.
  *Standardise on:* `overbound` for the direction word (it has a named partner, `runaway`), keeping `overreach` for the instrument alone.
  
  **V3 — `MISS` is a homonym across two ledgers that share one codec.** `darkness-ledger.txt:10` — *"MISS the grammar reads nothing of the line even with the construct standing alone — no rule"*. `ablation-ledger.txt:9` — *"MISS the grammar leaves this character plain and ablating it changes the host's tree shape"*. Both files are parsed by the same `ledger-shape.js`.
  *Standardise on:* `dark` for the line-grain fault and `unmarked` for the character-grain fault; keep `MISS` for neither.
  
  **V4 — four words for one lifecycle.** `stale` (a declaration whose finding no longer appears — 8 corpus and 24 tool files), `explains nothing` / `explaining nothing` (25 tool files, 1 corpus), `retires` (ceiling, delimiter, colour-pair), against `unruled` (15 tool files, 1 corpus) which names the **opposite** side — a finding no declaration covers.
  *Standardise on:* `idle` for a declaration explaining nothing, `unruled` for a finding nothing explains, `retired` for the act. `divergence-staleness.js` already uses `idle` (17 mentions of stale, and `:137` *"stands idle everywhere"`), so the word exists; it just has not won.
  
  **V5 — the reason prefix.** 8 prefixes in the rows: `OWED` (365), `READER` (149), `RULED` (5), `MEASURED` (4), `HELD` (3), `RE-SEATED` (2), `HOST` (1), `BEHAVIOUR` (1). Exactly two — `HOST` and `READER` — have a shared reader (`reader-scope.js`). The other six are read by eye.
  
  **V6 — `punctuation.definition` (444) against `punctuation.separator` (63) and `punctuation.section` (8)**, counted over `"name"`/`"contentName"` in `syntaxes/*.json`. `SCOPE-NAMES.md` rules four things (root first · punctuation stacks never nests · one segment one word · no borrowed language name) and **rules nothing about which punctuation sub-family a mark takes**. `scope-name-policy.test.js` checks three of the four and does not check this. I did not establish whether the 63 `punctuation.separator` uses answer a stated distinction; see §7.

  ## 7. Where I suspect a collapse would lose something and cannot prove it
  
  **(A) The 50-of-87 fixture overlap.** My measurement is over scope **vocabulary**, not scope-at-**position**. A snapshot pins where a scope lands; a fixture pins where a scope lands **with the intent written next to it**, and `tiddlywiki5.heading.tw5.test:28` is the shape: *"A HEADING'S TEXT IS MARKUP, NOT A DECLARED NAME. It keeps `entity.name.section`, the shape markdown publishes…"*. Retiring a fixture because a snapshot covers its drift trades a named law for a diff. `tests/memetic-wikitext/attic/README.md` already states this exact refusal: *"Rewriting these to assert whatever the base now reads would turn a test of INTENT into a record of BEHAVIOUR — the failure mode the snapshot literature names."* **I cannot tell which of the 50 carry a law and which carry only a reading.** That decision is YANG's.
  
  **(B) The colour cluster.** Nine gates, each whose header opens by distinguishing itself from the others: `colour-witness` *"Every other gate here reads scope NAMES"*; `construct-legibility` *"Every other colour instrument here reads SCOPES"*; `contrast-witness` *"reach and legibility name two different questions, and every instrument in this house measured the first"*; `dark-construct` *"Every other gate here asks whether two things read ALIKE or APART"*; `theme-collision` *"Nothing here ever asked `vscode-textmate` what it actually paints"*. Each cites a measurement where collapsing into its neighbour would have ruled a healthy grammar broken (`construct-legibility`: *"44 of 65 themes paint the containers identically … A gate built on containers would have ruled a healthy grammar broken"*). The shared anecdote (D3) and the shared resolver suggest fusion; **every header argues against it with a number, and I did not re-run the numbers.**
  
  **(C) `overreach` ×4.** `overreach` reads `tests/samples/*.tw`; `overreach-corpus-files` reads `corpus/**/*.tw`; `overreach-corpus-memetic` reads `corpus/memetic/*.mem`; `overreach-host` and `overreach-cut` read the host's own tiddlers at `--corpus 400`. All five share one `--expected=corpus/expected-divergence.txt`. The first two look like one glob. **I did not measure whether `tests/samples/*.tw` surfaces any divergence class `corpus/**/*.tw` does not** — that wants two `overreach-check` runs (minutes each), and `LEDGER-3.0.0.md:1352` warns the shape exists in the other direction: *"A LEDGER SERVES TWO SWEEPS. The widget-tag ruling reads idle over the 45-file corpus and explains 110 of the host's own carriers; retiring it on the narrower reading dropped the reach pass from 99.5% to 97.1%."*
  
  **(D) The three flag-pairs (D6) and the two-glob pair (D7).** Fusing six gates into three and two into one is trivially cheap. But `gate-report.js:101-107` keys the harvest on each gate's **own SUMMARY line**, and `GateReport.tid` reads `gates-held: 49 of 49`. Fusing changes the denominator and the per-arm verdicts a reader opens the report for. **Whether a reader needs `engine-behaviour`'s verdict apart from `engine-witness`'s, I cannot say from the code.**
  
  **(E) `carrier-ledger.txt` against `swallow-ledger.txt`.** Identical row grammar (`<direction> <key>   # reason`), identical direction vocabulary (`runaway` / `overbound`), one of 7 rows and one of 14. `carrier-ledger.txt:7-10` refuses the fusion in its own words: *"HELD APART FROM `swallow-ledger.txt` ON PURPOSE. That one rules what this corpus produces, and a ruling there explaining nothing fails its gate … A carrier class has no corpus specimen BY CONSTRUCTION, so it needs a ledger whose entries answer to different ground."* The reason reads sound. **I could not refute it, and I could not confirm that all 7 carrier rows genuinely lack a corpus specimen** — that wants a `still --reach` pass.
  
  **(F) `prose-reading-ledger.txt` against `PlainConstructs.tid`.** Same shape (scope → reason), two homes, one in `corpus/` and one in the wiki. `prose-reading-ledger.txt:8-11` refuses the fusion: *"HELD APART FROM `PlainConstructs`, WHICH RULES THE OTHER FAULT. That one rules a construct NO rule reaches; this one rules a construct a rule reaches and buys nothing for. The two cures differ … and a list fusing them sends a reader to the wrong repair."* The stated distinction is real in the instruments (`dark-construct` zero-reach · `contrast-witness` reached-and-quiet). **I did not verify the two populations are disjoint**; if a scope appears in both, the reason is weaker than it reads. One is 1 row and one is ~8 entries, so this is cheap to settle and I did not.
  
  **(G) `unasked-regions-ceiling.txt` (14) against `swallow-ledger.txt`.** The ceiling file states the parting itself: *"Standing open names no defect. Disagreeing does, and the ledger beside this file holds those."* Both written by `swallow-witness.js`. Coverage against correctness — the parting looks right. **I did not confirm the 97-region population the ceiling's prose cites.**
  
  **(H) The debt backlogs.** `ablation-ledger.txt`: 330 of 359 rows carry `OWED`. `darkness-ledger.txt`: 93 of 111. A ledger that is 92% owed either names a real, enumerated backlog or has become a list that records rather than guards. `ruling-breadth-ceiling.txt` already retired one guard for exactly this shape (*"A guard that re-seats on every honest change has stopped guarding"*). **I cannot tell which these are without reading the 423 reasons**, and the answer decides whether the two biggest corpus files collapse into counts or stay as rows.

Either a fifth unstated law exists and belongs in the one home, or the 63 uses are an accretion. **I did not read the 63 sites.**
  
  **(K) One possible contradiction I chased and retract.** The README's generated block says *"No construct reads as body text in more than a quarter of the 65 bundled themes"* while `prose-reading-ledger.txt`'s single row cites *"17 of 65 themes, one above this ledger's bar"*. I ran `node tools/reading-recipe.js` — its output matches the README byte for byte, and `BAR = 16` with 17 > 16 means the row sits above the bar and is therefore **ruled**, which is what keeps it out of the recipe. No contradiction. The two statements do depend on an unwelded 65 and an unwelded 16 (R3, R4).

No tracked file edited; `git status --short` shows `?? node_modules` and nothing else, verified at the end of this wave. Probe scratch under my own job tmp, `probe.vsix` removed. Nothing run that writes a tracked file.
  
  **For a reader with no access to this repository:** the project is a TextMate syntax grammar for TiddlyWiki wikitext plus a memetic dialect, shipped as a VS Code extension. Its harness is 49 npm-script "gates" over 35 instruments in `tools/`, 39 structural "invariants" (`tools/invariants/*.test.js`), 20 declaration files under `corpus/` (row-per-finding "ledgers" and single-number "floors"/"ceilings"), 40 pinned tokenization snapshots, and 89 hand-written assertion fixtures. Every number below says what it was measured over.
  
  ---
  
  ## PART A — The six measurements
  
  ### A1. `dark-construct` vs `contrast-witness` — SETTLED: two gates, not one
  
  Ran both with `--verbose` over the repository's own corpus and its 65 bundled themes; took each gate's printed finding set and intersected on the full scope name.
  
  - `dark-construct` — **22** scope names, derived over **340 host constructs × 65 themes**; summary line: `340 construct(s) over 65 themes, 22 plain, 0 unaccounted`.
  - `contrast-witness` — **26** scope names, derived over **278 scope stacks / 1378 prose readings × 65 themes**; summary line: `278 stack(s) over 65 theme(s), 1378 prose reading(s), 1 above the bar of 16, 0 unruled, 0 explaining nothing`.
  - **Union 47. Intersection 1.** 21 dark-only, 25 contrast-only. The single overlap is `meta.paragraph.tiddlywiki5`. Re-run at three-segment-prefix granularity (to catch a match hidden by a language suffix): still exactly 1.
  
  **2.1% overlap.** The axis YANG defends is not merely empirical, it is structural: `dark-construct` reports a construct **no theme rule reaches**, `contrast-witness` reports a scope **a theme rule reaches and paints the editor's own foreground anyway**. A scope cannot sit in both categories *for the same theme*. `meta.paragraph` appears in both only because the two gates count different populations of themes (dark: 9 of 65 colour it, so 56 have no rule; contrast: 12 of 65 reach-and-waste it). **Fusing these two gates would lose 46 of 47 findings.**
  
  **YANG said it would take my measurement. The measurement says: keep both.** My wave-one duplicate-intent claim D3 is reduced to its true size — the two tools duplicate a *sentence*, not a *measurement*. Both headers carry the same provenance anecdote nearly verbatim (`theme-parity.js:5` and `dark-construct.js:6`, both "a heading did exactly that — 9 of 65 themes coloured its text … every gate read green, because a scope stood there and matched its siblings"). That is 2 lines of duplicated prose with one home available, and nothing more.
  
  ### A2. `prose-reading-ledger.txt` vs `PlainConstructs.tid` — SETTLED: disjoint, but weakly tested
  
  Listed both declaration surfaces.
  
  - `editions/tw5-syntax/tiddlers/PlainConstructs.tid` — **20** keys (`meta.paragraph`, `meta.element.inline.math`, `meta.element.structure.svg`, `meta.link.wikilink`, `meta.multids.text.html`, `meta.tiddle.field.text.plain…`, `meta.text.tiddler.fields`, four `markup.list.*`, `markup.list.listquote.quote`, five `markup.other.table*`, `markup.other.style`, `markup.underline`, `markup.link.tiddlywiki5`). Sole reader: `dark-construct.js`.
  - `corpus/prose-reading-ledger.txt` — **1** row: `markup.other.value.lar.memetic-wikitext`. Readers: `contrast-witness.js`, `reading-recipe.js`.
  - **Intersection 0.**
  
  Two caveats a consolidating reader needs. (i) With 20 entries against 1, disjointness is close to trivial and tests the stated axis very little. (ii) The axis is nonetheless sound for the reason in A1 — the two populations are structurally exclusive per theme, not merely separate today. And the sizing checks out in both directions: `dark-construct` reports `22 plain, 0 unaccounted` against 20 declarations (the three `meta.element.inline.math.{mn,mi,mo}` findings collapse under one declaration, as does `meta.element.structure.svg`), and `contrast-witness` reports `1 above the bar of 16, 0 unruled, 0 explaining nothing` against 1 row at 17 of 65 themes. **Both declaration surfaces are exactly sized to their findings. Neither carries a dead entry.**
  
  What remains of my wave-one D5 complaint is narrower and still true: these two surfaces live in **two different homes** — one a JSON data tiddler inside a TiddlyWiki edition, one a plain-text file under `corpus/` — and one gate (`colour-witness.js`) reads declarations from both at once (`ReaderRelations.tid` for its "must read apart" list, `corpus/colour-pair-ledger.txt` + `corpus/colour-pair-floor.txt` for its findings). The *split by fault* is right; the *split by storage* is arbitrary.
  
  ### A3. `carrier-ledger.txt`'s 7 rows — SETTLED: the defence holds, over corpus ground
  
  `corpus/carrier-ledger.txt` records divergence classes the *memetic carriers outside this repository* surface, and its header claims they have no corpus specimen "BY CONSTRUCTION". Ran `still.js --over ./corpus --reach --verbose` — the whole-corpus arm, no sampling.
  
  Result: `reach  52 of 52 carrier(s) stand fully named, 100.0% (floor 99.5%); 5 carrier(s) no cut reads, 186 divergence(s), 0 class(es) blocking`.
  
  **Zero classes blocking over corpus ground.** Every one of the 186 divergences the corpus produces falls inside a `swallow-ledger.txt` ruling; none required a `carrier-ledger.txt` row to be explained. That is consistent with the header's claim and is the strongest evidence a corpus-only pass can give. **Not proof** — proving the 7 rows each lack a corpus specimen needs the host sweep (`still --host --reach`, ~4403 carriers) and I did not run it. What I can say: over 52 corpus files and 100% named coverage, the corpus ledger was never consulted. The parting stands.
  
  ### A4. `overreach`'s two glob arms — STRUCK
  
  YANG's measurement (per-arm exclusive rulings over the 111 in `corpus/expected-divergence.txt`: `overreach` 31 · `overreach-corpus-files` 57 · `overreach-corpus-memetic` 2 · `overreach-host` 2 · `overreach-cut` 0 · union 101 · 10 unused) already made the case. I checked the two mechanical facts that decide whether the fusion is even expressible, and they close it:
  
  1. **`overreach-check.js:306`** — `const pattern = args.find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'))`. The tool takes the **first** non-flag argument as *the* pattern and ignores any second. Line 380 hands it to `bash -c "ls ${pattern}"`. **One glob per invocation, by signature.** The two arms read `./tests/samples/*.tw` and `./corpus/**/*.tw` — two directories, not expressible as one `ls` pattern.
  2. **`divergence-staleness.js:48-51`** — `derivedRuns(scripts)` filters `package.json`'s own `scripts` for bodies matching `/overreach-check\.js/` that carry `--expected=corpus/expected-divergence.txt`. **The staleness run set IS the manifest.** Remove a script entry and that arm's population leaves the union; rulings explained only there become "explaining nothing", the gate calls them stale, and the ledger's discipline retires them.
  
  So fusing the two arms is not a glob edit — it needs a tool change, and done naively it retires either 31 or 57 written rulings. The gain was one gate out of 49. **My wave-one collapse candidate is struck.** YANG's finding kills it; I am not defending it.
  
  ### A5. Collapse #11, `swallow-witness` ⊂ `still` — STRUCK
  
  I ranked this highest-risk in wave one on the strength of `still.js:35-38`'s own comment: *"Pointed at `./corpus` this pass found 8 classes, every one already named, and `swallow-witness` finds the same 8 over the same files with the same comparison."* I ran both over that identical ground.
  
  `swallow-witness.js --verbose` → `1689 cut(s) across 52 corpus file(s), 10 quote(s) closed to ask, 13 divergence(s), 0 recorded, 0 unruled, 1 answering the host sweep, 0 ruling(s) explaining nothing`. Its 13 classes with instance counts: `overbound italic` 82 · `overbound codeinline` 24 · `overbound underscore` 19 · `runaway meta.directive.variable.*` 18 · `runaway comment.*` 9 · `overbound bold` 8 · `runaway meta.embedded.*` 7 · `overbound conditional` 5 · `overbound html` 5 · `runaway meta.directive.parameters.*` 4 · `runaway meta.element.*` 2 · `runaway meta.tag.widget.*` 2 · `runaway meta.transclusion.*` 1.

  **82+24+19+18+9+8+7+5+5+4+2+2+1 = 186.** The two agree on the population exactly — and the agreement is *why they are not one gate*: `still` reports the 186 **instances** and ratchets a *coverage share* against `corpus/carrier-reach-floor.txt` plus a *ruling-breadth* bound against `corpus/ruling-breadth-ceiling.txt`; `swallow-witness` reports the 13 **classes** and in the same run produces two readings `still` never prints:
  
  - `regions: 97 carry no line bound, 83 stand open under some cut, 14 go unasked (ceiling 14)` — the sole source of `corpus/unasked-regions-ceiling.txt`, a *coverage* ratchet about regions no cut ever opens;

  My wave-one claim that `syntaxes/attic/` ships was an inference from reading `package-contents.js`. I observed it instead.

  ```
  tw5.png · package.json · memetic-language-configuration.json · language-configuration.json
  contributing.md · ThirdPartyNotices.txt · SCOPE-NAMES.md · README.md · MIGRATION.md
  LICENSE · LEDGER-3.0.0.md · CHANGELOG.md
  syntaxes/{tw5-tid-file,tw5-test-file,tw5-substitution-injection,
    tw5-substituted-attribute-injection,tw5-multids-file,tw5-fields,
    toml.tw5-syntax,tiddlywiki5,memetic-wikitext}.json
  snippets/{tiddler-fields,snippets}.json
  docs/scope-naming-prior-art.mem · docs/differential-test-design.mem
  syntaxes/attic/memetic-wikitext.sketch.json      ← 14 013 bytes, retired grammar
  syntaxes/attic/README.md                          ←    936 bytes
  docs/prior-art/{treesitter-and-semantic-tokens,synthesis,sublime-vs-textmate,
    paint-and-delimiters,library-highlighters,fixed-vocabularies,coordinator-direct}.mem
  ```
  
  **Confirmed.** And larger than I had seen: the exclusion file `.vscodeignore` names neither `syntaxes/attic` nor `docs/` (`grep -cE "^docs|attic"` → 0), so the package also carries **seven prior-art design documents under `docs/prior-art/` totalling 280 996 bytes**, which I had not enumerated in wave one. Weighted: the 9 shipped `.mem` documents plus the attic total **349 604 bytes**.
  
  The distinction a consolidating reader should hold: `.vscodeignore`'s own header rules that *"The published extension carries the grammars, the snippets, the language configuration and its documentation."* The record documents (`README`, `CHANGELOG`, `LEDGER`, `MIGRATION`, `SCOPE-NAMES`, `contributing`) ship **by that intent**. The `docs/prior-art/` set is arguably documentation too. **`syntaxes/attic/` fits neither clause** — it is a grammar the editor never loads, and `syntaxes/attic/README.md` says so itself: *"Nothing in `package.json` names it, no gate reads it, and no editor opens under it."* True of *loading*. Packaging is a different question that sentence does not answer, and nothing asks it: `package-contents.js:35-45` compares **manifest → package** only, never **package → needed**.

  ## PART B — The four reckonings
  
  ### B1. Does one fix serve `every-gate-collides` and `one-implementation`? — No: one rule, two edits
  
  I reproduced YANG's false green from the source rather than relaying it.
  
  `tools/invariants/every-gate-collides.test.js`: line 67 reads each test file into `text` with `fs.readFileSync` — **raw**. Line 43 defines `code = text.replace(comments away)`. Lines 44-48 test five collider clauses (`runProvoked|runInSandbox`, `notStrictEqual(code, 0)`, `assert.throws`, `.length, [1-9]`, `assert.ok(x.length >`) against **`code`**. Lines 77-78 then evaluate `named.test(s.text) && collides(s.text)` — **the name half against raw text, the collider half against stripped code, as two independent predicates over one file.** A file naming the tool only inside a comment, which happens to carry any collider clause for its own unrelated subject, satisfies both halves. YANG's `theme-collision` case is the live instance.
  
  `tools/invariants/one-implementation.test.js:33`: `const sources = all.filter((s) => !s.name.endsWith('.test.js'))` — the duplication scan **excludes every test file**, so duplication inside test files is invisible. Live instances I measured in wave one: a byte-identical `scopesOn` helper in `tools/invariants/image-attribute-list.test.js` and `attribute-value-across-lines.test.js` (same md5 over the function body), and the incantation `source ./grammars.sh` — the exact work this invariant's own rule table assigns to `tokenizer.js` — inlined at `memetic-containment.test.js:37` and `memetic-superset.test.js:36`.

# YIN wave two (for the blind reader) — the seams, settled
All numbers are YIN's own measurements, stated with what they were measured over.

## Measurements that settled a seam
A1 dark-construct vs contrast-witness: 22 findings vs 26, UNION 47, INTERSECTION 1
  (meta.paragraph.tiddlywiki5 only, and only because the two count different theme populations:
  9 of 65 colour it, 12 of 65 reach-and-waste it). Structurally exclusive per theme — a scope cannot
  be both unreached and reached-but-quiet in one theme. Fusing would lose 46 of 47 findings. KEEP BOTH.
  What survives of YIN's wave-one claim: 2 lines of duplicated anecdote prose in two tool headers.
A2 prose-reading-ledger (1 row) vs PlainConstructs.tid (20 keys): INTERSECTION 0. Both surfaces
  exactly sized to their findings; neither carries a dead entry. Split by FAULT is right; split by
  STORAGE (a corpus text file vs a JSON data tiddler, with colour-witness reading one of each) is
  arbitrary.
A3 carrier-ledger's 7 rows: `still --over ./corpus --reach` reads 52 of 52 carriers fully named,
  100.0% (floor 99.5%), 186 divergences, 0 classes blocking — the corpus ledger was never consulted.
  Consistent with its header's claim; not proof (wants the ~4403-carrier host sweep).
A4 overreach's two glob arms: STRUCK. overreach-check.js:306 takes the FIRST non-flag argument as
  the only pattern (handed to `bash -c "ls …"`), so two directories cannot be one glob;
  divergence-staleness.js:48-51 derives its run set FROM package.json, so dropping a script entry
  retires that arm's exclusive rulings (31 and 57 by YANG's count).
A5 swallow-witness ⊂ still: STRUCK. Over the same corpus ground the two agree exactly —
  swallow's 13 classes sum to 186 instances (82+24+19+18+9+8+7+5+5+4+2+2+1) and still reports 186.
  The agreement is WHY they are two gates: still ratchets a coverage share (carrier-reach-floor) and
  a ruling-breadth bound; swallow alone produces unasked-regions-ceiling (97 regions carry no line
  bound, 83 open under some cut, 14 unasked) and an 18-region probe-escape reading. What survives:
  still.js:35-38 says the pass finds 8 classes; it finds 13 — a stale comment that caused YIN to rank
  a destructive collapse highest in wave one.
A6 the .vsix: CONFIRMED by observation (`vsce ls --no-dependencies`, 34 files). syntaxes/attic ships
  (sketch grammar 14,013 bytes + README 936). Larger than wave one saw: docs/prior-art ships too,
  seven design documents, 280,996 bytes; nine shipped .mem documents plus the attic total 349,604
  bytes. .vscodeignore names neither attic nor docs. package-contents.js:35-45 checks manifest →
  package only, never package → needed.

## Reckonings
B1 One rule, two edits: every-gate-collides pairs a NAME match over RAW text with a CLAUSE match over
  comment-stripped code (lines 67/77), a GRAIN fault; one-implementation:33 excludes *.test.js, a
  POPULATION fault. corpus-ledgers.test.js:43 and :33-39 are the worked examples for both.
  Cost asymmetry: the first edit will red at least one currently-green gate; the second WIDENS
  obligations and needs a written allowance list.
B2 gate-report --check writes two tracked files: textmate-ceiling.js --write → TextMateCeiling.tid,
  and builtins-sync.js (no --check in the manifest) → syntaxes/tiddlywiki5.json, a SHIPPED grammar.
  Law that generalises: a harvest's CHECK arm belongs in the manifest, its WRITE arm never does.
  Precedent already correct twice: edition:build/edition:check and signals/signals:check.
B3 CI's "not redundancy" ruling covers the four previously-continue-on-error gates (signals:check,
  overreach-host, overreach-cut, upstream-coverage), NOT compose. The grammar job's apparent
  duplicates are defended by a four-way OS/node matrix; the compose job runs ubuntu/node22 — the same
  platform as gates. Platform coverage is the dividing line; compose is the only true duplicate job.
B4 Collision obligations: 21 of 39 invariants carry a recognised collider, 18 do not — and
  structurally NO invariant ever enters the pairing, since every-gate-collides pairs test files
  against GATE TOOL NAMES. The exemption is by construction and nothing records it.
  Items that move an obligation: the shared owedOf() (must carry delimiter-inheritance.test.js:104-107's
  collider across), lifting one-implementation's exclusion (adds obligations), fusing snap-tid+snap-meta
  (moves a denominator nobody publishes), the sentinel fusion (revised), the corpus renames, and the
  attic item — which must land with the first collider package-contents.js has ever had.

## Wave-two list
CONFIRMED: delete run_snapshots.sh + echo-test + list-test (zero readers) · strike four narrowing test
aliases (82 scripts → 75) · one owedOf() beside readerOf() (five ad-hoc /^OWED/ sites; bracket-witness
and light-cone do not strip the READER prefix; 76 live READER…OWED rows, all in darkness-ledger) ·
two edits for one rule (B1) · syntaxes/attic out of the package (C5, with a collider for
package-contents) · strike the CI compose job (B3) · one home for the migration headline, fixing two
restatements that say 111 where the certified figure is 110 (MIGRATION:36, SCOPE-NAMES:20) and noting
LEDGER:1294's drifted 585/122/247 · weld the theme count and derive BAR from it (five instruments
hardcode node_modules/tm-themes with no override, so the weld must read "65 as this repository
bundles them") · fix four wrong present-tense counts (corpus-ledgers "Thirteen" vs 20, GateReport-Doc
"Seventeen" vs 49/35/65, theme-model.test "Four gates" vs 12 requirers, tokenizer.test "Twenty-two"
vs 26) without deleting the paragraphs · true still.js's 8 → 13 · MISS → dark/unmarked (one codec,
two ledgers, one homonym).
REVISED: share the two orphan sentinel STRINGS only, never the two baseline derivations (oracle
readAt vs a written control file — two of five containment grains) · generate the README's
completeness CHECK, keep the curated prose, put only a --check arm in the manifest (25 distinct names,
3 duplicated bullets, 37 of 49 gates unnamed, the weld asserting only existence) · move
gate-report.js:18-25's archaeology to LEDGER:1809-1812, which already holds it — a move, never a
delete · snap-tid+snap-meta stays weakest-defended but do the collider fix first ·
corpus file naming to -ledger/-ratchet with direction in the first comment line · one lifecycle
vocabulary (idle / unruled / retired), the winner already present in divergence-staleness:137.
STRUCK: swallow ⊂ still · dark-construct ∪ contrast-witness · the overreach glob fusion ·
prose-reading-ledger ∪ PlainConstructs.

## What YANG made visible to YIN
The invariants' structural exemption from the collider requirement · package-contents as a blocking
untested gate that C5 depends on · the 10 unused rulings being exactly the 10 READER 5.5.0-prerelease
ones, keyed out by the same module owedOf() would extend, 4 of them OWED · flags that switch
POPULATION rather than output, which withdraws all three "one tool two gates" candidates ·
backtrack-witness's wall-clock sensitivity, which any item changing what-runs-beside-what can move ·
both record welds reading the UNRELEASED section only, so new welds must key on something else.

## Not verified this wave
No gate-report --check (writes two tracked files) · no .vsix extraction (listing only) · no
still --host --reach · no test-tools · the 63 punctuation.separator sites unread · the 423 OWED rows
unread (330 of 359 in ablation-ledger, 93 of 111 in darkness-ledger) — deciding whether those two
largest corpus files are an enumerated backlog or a guard that stopped guarding · four of YANG's
seams not taken up: overreach-cut's 0 exclusives, canary-memetic vs memetic-containment, the four
colour-reader CLI surfaces, the 6 invisible attic fixtures.

The fixtures: vocabulary is the wrong measure, and I can show it **My measurement, with method.** I extracted the scope vocabulary of all 40 `.snap` snapshot files (**737 distinct scopes**) and of all 87 assertion fixtures, then counted fixtures whose asserted vocabulary is wholly contained in the snapshot vocabulary. The `.snap` format records what IS present; it has no syntax for absence. **Any fixture carrying a negative is categorically irreplaceable by a snapshot, at any vocabulary.** Of my 60 vocabulary-subset fixtures, **29 carry negatives.** **(ii) Construct presence, which is not vocabulary presence.** A fixture's scopes can all appear in some snapshot while the *construct* appears in no sample at all — because the same scopes are emitted by other constructs. I tested this on the two densest candidates and the result is decisive. `tiddlywiki5.macro-dynamic-params.tw5.test` pins **76 assertions** over seven forms of a call's parameter *value*. I grepped all 40 sample carriers for each form: | parameter-value form | sample carriers holding it | |---|---| | `<

>` (filtered) | **0** | | `<

>` (indirect) | **0** | | `<

>` (multi-valued variable) | **0** | | `` <

> `` (backtick substitution) | **0** | | ```` <

> ```` (triple backtick) | **0** | | `<

>>>` (a nested call as the value) | **0** | | `<

>` | 2 | **Six of seven forms appear in zero snapshot samples.** Three of them (`{{{}}}`, `((v))`, and `{{t!!f}}`) appear in zero broad-corpus files either, so neither the coverage gate nor the overreach gates read them. That fixture is the **only** place in the repository where those readings are pinned. And the nested-call form is under an active debt row in the release ledger (which records a call's `=` before a nested value as OWED), so deleting the fixture would orphan a live ruling. **I corrected myself mid-measurement and report it:** my first grep said `macro-string-params`'s named-argument forms (`<

>` / `<

>`) appeared in no sample. That was a too-narrow pattern. Re-grepped: samples carry **14** named-argument calls. So `macro-string-params` **is** snapshot-covered at the construct level, and its 61 assertions are the kind of pin a snapshot already holds. **THE SPLIT, ruled per fixture.** Of the 60 adding no novel vocabulary: - **29 carry negative assertions** → LAW. Un-snapshotable by format. Densest: `tiddlywiki5.styleblock-closer` (15 assertions, **all 15 negative**), `tiddlywiki5.heading` (8 negatives), `sigil-marker.mem.test` (7), `tiddlywiki5.mvv-attributes` (6), `tiddlywiki5.argument-surface` (5 negatives + 27 prose lines), `tiddlywiki5.table-markers` (4), `fence-reads-as-its-meta.mem.test` (4), `tiddlywiki5.image-source` (4). - **22 more carry explanatory prose but no negatives** → LAW, held by the prose beside the assertion. Examples with their prose-line counts: `lar-texture-restack.mem.test` (13), `sigil-verb-and-bearing.mem.test` (12), `raw-delimiters` (11), `tiddlywiki5.definition-kinds` (9), `lar-root-terms.mem.test` (9), `tiddlywiki5.code-reads-literally` (8), `gradient-floor.mem.test` (8). - **9 carry neither negatives nor prose.** I read all nine.
